messages:
Sam (eng-platform): Quick sync — we need to pick a single canonical correlation key for the new inference dashboards. My proposal: use the W3C traceparent.trace-id as the primary join key, and also propagate X-Request-Id for human-friendly lookups. Anyone opposed?
Maya (eng-runtime): +1 to trace-id as canonical. OTEL libs already emit traceparent so we can surface trace_id in logs/metrics. Only caution: our batcher sometimes creates internal sub-spans without propagating traceparent to each sub-request — we need to fix that.
Kevin (eng-infra): We still have a mix: some services set x-request-id, others set x-correlation-id. I can add a lightweight header-middleware that does: if traceparent exists derive trace-id -> set X-Redwood-Trace, else generate traceparent and set X-Redwood-Trace. Also copy or set X-Request-Id if missing.
Olivia (product-analytics): For dashboards we need these fields available in the telemetry surface: trace_id, request_id, root_span_id, sampled (bool), route, model_variant, gpu_type, and latency_ms. Trace_id will let us join traces to logs and spans. Request_id helps SRE/customer-support searches.
Sam (eng-platform): Concrete header plan suggestion (pseudo):
```
# service middleware
if not req.headers['traceparent']:
  req.headers['traceparent'] = generate_w3c_traceparent()
trace_id = parse_traceparent(req.headers['traceparent']).trace_id
req.headers['x-redwood-trace'] = trace_id  # canonical short key for dashboards
if not req.headers['x-request-id']:
  req.headers['x-request-id'] = uuid4()
```
Maya (eng-runtime): That looks good. Also: for internal batching where one GPU call serves N logical requests, create sub-span per logical request with attribute "sub_request_id" (uuid) and tag parent trace_id. This ensures dashboards can show per-user latency while traces show kernel/serving latency.
Kevin (eng-infra): Sampling policy thoughts: default global 1% sample, but force-sample 100% for error responses (>=500), high-latency (>300ms), and any canary/rollout traffic. Also provide debug sampling toggle per customer id. We need to expose these triggers to tracing agent config.
Olivia (product-analytics): For dashboards we want derived metrics too: p50/p95 request latency by model_variant, trace-sampled-rate, and proportion of traces that include an infer_span vs only request-span. If sampling skews per-route we must store sample_rate per metric row so we can adjust estimates.
Sam (eng-platform): Important: pick one join key for dashboards queries. I vote X-Redwood-Trace (trace_id) — shorter, consistent. x-request-id remains accessible for logs. Any objections?
Maya (eng-runtime): No objections. One operational note: ensure the local dev environment (docker-compose) injects traceparent so dev traces match prod. Otherwise we lose coverage for batch logic.
Kevin (eng-infra): I'll open a PR to add middleware in shared-infra-lib and a sidecar env var to enable "force-traceparent" for legacy services. Plan: land infra PR by EOD Friday.
Sam (eng-platform): Nice. We should also add a small section to the dashboard docs about the two keys and how to search/join.
Olivia (product-analytics): I'll update the dashboard spec: list of required fields and sampling metadata. Dropping a short example query for metrics team once headers are standard.
Sam (eng-platform): Action items:
- Kevin: infra-middleware PR to set traceparent + X-Redwood-Trace and copy/generate X-Request-Id (due Fri)
- Maya: runtime changes to propagate traceparent into batch sub-spans + add sub_request_id tagging (due next Wed)
- Olivia: dashboard schema update + example queries (due next Tue)
- Sam: docs + console UX note about showing trace link in the trace drawer (due next Tue)
deploy-bot: deploy started for shared-infra-lib-canary (build 2025.7.42) :rocket:
Kevin (eng-infra): deploy-bot says canary started. I'll monitor sampling/headers in logs. If we see >0.1% missing trace_id after canary we roll back.
Maya (eng-runtime): I'll add unit tests for trace propagation in batching harness.
Olivia (product-analytics): Thanks — once infra canary is healthy I'll re-run the dashboard join tests.
Sam (eng-platform): Thanks all. We'll reconvene after canary. :thumbsup:
